title: Hosting strategy & budget sprint - Maelstrom Energy
summary: Discovery call to map Maelstrom's expected throughput for inference, explore per-token cost levers (batching, KV cache), and align on pilot budget and hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC). Customer is bandwidth-constrained in budget, needs SSO and audit logs, and is interested in a 6-week pilot with benchmarks. SE requested sample traces; AE to send pricing + pilot SOW.
next_steps: Ethan - Send pilot pricing spreadsheet and SOW template by 2026-11-27
Priya - Share recommended batching and KV cache config and sample perf traces (p50/p95) by 2026-11-30
Tom - Provide sample traffic profile and peak qps by 2026-11-26
action_items: Ethan Chen - Send pilot pricing and contract SOW - 2026-11-27
Priya Rao - Export perf traces for our 13B model baseline - 2026-11-30
Tom Keller - Share 2 weeks of production-like traffic csv - 2026-11-26
Aisha Grant - Loop in legal for procurement timeline - 2026-12-01
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-23 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Tom Keller (Head of ML, Maelstrom), Diane Wu (Platform Eng), Rajiv Menon (Dir Data Science), Aisha Grant (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick intake to align on hosting tradeoffs and budget. Customer budget strongly constrained, wants clear unit economics for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Wants pilot to prove per-token costs and tail latency under their workloads.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? we just have a tight agenda: understand your usage profile, constraints, and pilot scope.
[00:18] Tom (Maelstrom): yeah hi, tom here. we run inference for forecasting and anomaly detection, mostly short prompts but some long context for batch runs. our main ask: can you help us figure out cost per inference and the hosting path that makes sense under our budget.
[00:35] Diane (Maelstrom): and hi from infra, we care about VPC options, audit logs, and SSO.
[00:42] Ethan: great. priya from our side will dig into perf and batching details. priya?
[00:46] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all. quick note — i want to capture peak qps, average tokens per call, and percent long-running requests. that drives whether batching and KV cache help.
[01:05] Rajiv (Maelstrom): our numbers: avg qps 15, peak 110, avg tokens per call ~320, top 5% are 2k tokens (historical). we do a lot of short chat-like stuff plus nightly bulk annotation.
[01:25] Priya: ok that's helpful. with that profile, there are three big levers for unit cost: per-token price (hosted), continuous batching (reduces GPU overhead), and KV/prefix cache for repeated context.
[01:40] Tom: can you quantify. like, hosted per-token versus running dedicated? we've seen public numbers but need realistic delta for our workload.
[01:48] Ethan: sure — rough ballpark: hosted API per-token list price for a 13B-ish open model is X, but effective cost can be 30-60% lower with batching and caching depending on request mix. dedicated moves fixed cost to reserved GPU pool — you pay monthly commit but unit price decreases as throughput increases. private (VPC/on-prem) adds infra + ops cost up-front, so that's best if you need data residency or reeeally strict control.
[02:15] Aisha (Maelstrom): when you say "per-token list price X" can you send actual numbers? procurement needs line items.
[02:21] Ethan: yes we'll send a pilot pricing spreadsheet. for confidentiality i won't read list here, but we'll model your QPS and token mix in the sheet.
[02:29] Diane: how does batching affect latency? our SLO is 200ms p95 for short prompts.
[02:35] Priya: good question. batching increases throughput and lowers per-token cost but adds headroom for latency. Redwood's continuous batching can be tuned: you can cap batch wait time at 10ms or 30ms. for short prompts we can often keep p95 under 200ms while still benefiting from micro-batching. it's a tradeoff.
[02:53] Rajiv: and KV cache — what's realistic? we have a lot of repeated prefix for customers, can that save tokens?
[02:58] Priya: yes, KV/prefix caching stores cached activations for repeated context. in our tests for similar horizontal workload we saw 20-50% token reduction on repeated calls, which is huge. but effectiveness depends on cache hit rate; you need stable prefixes.
[03:15] Tom: would the cache be in our VPC for private? also encryption?
[03:20] Ethan: for Private/VPC, yes cache and KV stay inside your network — and we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. for Hosted we provide encrypted cache but it's in Redwood-managed infra; we can do dedicated tenancy too.
[03:34] Aisha: SOC2? audit logs? those are must-haves for our procurement to sign off.
[03:39] Ethan: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, we have SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs. for private installs we can also integrate with on-prem HSM/KMS. we'll attach the security pack.
[03:52] Diane: circling back to dedicated sizing — if we reserved N GPUs, how do we estimate required number for peak 110 qps?
[03:59] Priya: depends on model and sequence lengths. for a 13B we typically get approx ~X tokens per second on an A100-like instance with continuous batching. let me be clear: i will run a sizing sim once we have token distribution and target p95.
[04:17] Tom: when you say "run a sim"— do you need traces? what format?
[04:21] Priya: ideally a 2-week trace csv with timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_id, endpoint. anonymized is fine. we use that to estimate batching gains and cost.
[04:34] Rajiv: ok we can pull that. ops: we estimate sending that to you by thursday.
[04:40] Ethan: perfect. on pilot length — teams usually do 4-8 weeks. with your security requirements and procurement, i'd budget 6 weeks. pilot includes a baseline run on hosted (or dedicated if you prefer), then tuning batching/cache, and a final benchmark report.
[05:00] Aisha: procurement wants pilot cost hard number. is there a nominal fee for pilot?
[05:05] Ethan: we typically waive platform fees for a short pilot but ask for a committed monthly min for dedicated. depends on route. i'll include options in the pricing sheet: hosted trial (usage-based) vs dedicated pilot (reserved with credit).
[05:19] Diane: one more infra question — what about fallback? if dedicated pool hits capacity spikes, do you route to hosted?
[05:27] Priya: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible hosted variant or smaller model; policies are configurable per route. that helps with graceful degradation during peaks.
[05:37] Tom: that fallback sounds critical. if we rely on dedicated but have unpredictable spikes, we need a predictable cost when falling back.
[05:44] Ethan: we can set a cap on fallback usage and predefine unit pricing for fallback to bound costs. we'll show examples in the SOW.
[05:52] Rajiv: earlier you mentioned quantization. would that affect accuracy? we have some QA thresholds.
[05:56] Priya: quantization (4-bit/8-bit) can reduce memory and increase throughput; some models show minimal quality drop, but we run evals against your prompt set. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and measure eval regressions.
[06:12] Tom: do you run A/B tests for rollouts? we want canary behavior.
[06:16] Ethan: yes rollouts are first-class: canary, A/B, automatic fallback. you can pin model versions.
[06:21] Aisha: timeline for procurement? we need a contract by mid-december ideally.
[06:25] Ethan: doable. pilot in early december, SOW and pricing by Friday, procurement review the week after.
[06:32] Diane: ok what about data residency in EU? half our customers are EU-based.
[06:36] Ethan: hosted has region options; Dedicated can be provisioned in specific regions; Private gets you full residency. we'll capture regional needs in the sheet.
[06:45] Rajiv: any cost expectations for KV cache hit rate of ~30%?
[06:49] Priya: a 30% hit rate often maps to 15-25% effective token cost reduction depending on model tokenization and sequence lengths. we'll model it exactly once we have traces.
[06:59] Tom: ok let's role-play numbers quick — say hosted effective per-token $0.0009 after our discounts, dedicated effective unit cost can drop to $0.0004 with full utilization — is that in the ballpark?
[07:10] Ethan: those are plausible ballpark numbers for that class of model. final numbers depend on committed capacity, burst allowances, and caching.
[07:20] Aisha: do you have references or customers in energy vertical?
[07:24] Ethan: we have several in logistics and retail; i'll ask for a reference call. energy-specific references are limited but we can share case studies on forecasts and anomaly detection.
[07:34] Diane: are there auto-scaling options for dedicated pools during seasonal spikes? we don't want to over-commit in quiet months.
[07:41] Priya: dedicated can be configured with burst capacity and policies that scale pods across instance types; we also have pre-defined fallbacks to hosted. autoscaling has cooldowns so you'd want to plan for expected spike patterns.
[07:55] Rajiv: what's the observability surface? we need per-token cost, per-route latency, per-user tracing.
[08:00] Ethan: Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and traces. we can also forward logs to your SIEM.
[08:10] Tom: ok — what do you need from us today to get the pilot priced?
[08:14] Priya: three things: 2-week traffic trace, desired SLO targets (p50/p95), and pilot scope (hosted-only vs dedicated evaluation vs private stack).
[08:22] Tom: we can deliver traces and SLOs; for scope we prefer to evaluate hosted->dedicated path first.
[08:29] Ethan: good. we'll set up a quick follow-up to walk the pricing sheet. proposed dates?
[08:33] Aisha: let's do Friday morning for a pricing walkthrough.
[08:36] Ethan: i'll send calendar invite.
[08:38] Diane: one more note: our security team may ask for a data processing addendum; is that standard?
[08:42] Ethan: yes DPA and security pack included. for Private installs we can do tailored agreements.
[08:46] Rajiv: what about model variants? can we run a smaller model at high qps and fall back to larger for critical requests?
[08:51] Priya: yep — routing by policy: latency-first for critical, cost-first for background. you can tag routes and set fallbacks.
[09:00] Tom: this is helpful. i want a concrete example in your SOW: baseline hosted run with micro-batching, then one dedicated node test, then a final delta report.
[09:08] Ethan: noted. we'll include a three-phase pilot plan.
[09:12] Aisha: procurement will want a clear exit or conversion path and estimated monthly TCO if we convert to dedicated.
[09:19] Ethan: we'll model conversion economics in the pilot wrap-up doc.
[09:24] Diane: ok thanks. i do have a quick question about tokenization and how bytes map to tokens for our telemetry.
[09:29] Priya: we can help with a tokenization mapping script to approximate tokens from bytes. we'll include that.
[09:34] Tom: anything else from your side?
[09:37] Priya: i'll try to sketch expected batching savings for your traffic right now — rough numbers only.
[09:41] Ethan: action items and next steps recap?
[09:44] Ethan: (recap) 1) Maelstrom to send 2-week trace and SLOs by 2026-11-26. 2) Redwood to send pricing sheet and SOW by 2026-11-27. 3) Priya to run sizing sim and send perf traces by 2026-11-30. 4) Pricing walkthrough Friday morning (Ethan to send invite).
[10:10] Aisha: sounds good, thanks.
[10:14] Tom: thanks all. we'll get the trace to you.
[52:00] Meeting end.
